scene.title: Electron shells of carbon
scene.summary: Carbon (Z=6) has two electron shells: 2 electrons in the first shell and 4 in the second.

beats.title: Carbon atom outline
beats.narration: We start with a carbon nucleus and its two concentric electron shells, empty for now.

beats.title: First shell filled
beats.narration: The innermost shell (n=1) holds exactly two electrons.

beats.title: Second shell filled
beats.narration: The outer shell (n=2) contains the remaining four electrons.

beats.title: Answer revealed
beats.narration: The second shell indeed holds the most electrons, completing carbon’s 2‑4 configuration.

beats.title: Recap
beats.narration: Carbon’s electron configuration is 1s² 2s² 2p²: 2 electrons in shell 1, 4 in shell 2.
